name: Out of Your Way
tagline: Some people send their love. You bring it.
epigraph: This cocktail is made at room temperature. Some things shouldn't arrive cold.
glassware: stemmed red wine glass (about 250 ml), at room temperature, no ice
language_row: Wren's Resonance on reading v4: ready. The 4-gram check is clean against every pour; six echoes were fixed in v1 (*Any Day*, *Fair Measure*, *Till Spring*, *Nothing to It*, *In Your Own Hand*, *Before the Room*), and five stock phrases were cut in v2. There's no "turning up" (*Any Day*), "already" or "ask" (*Hoping You'd Come*), and no gendered words about the guest. The she/her/he/his warnings in yours 1–4 are Bly, the Vernes and Bly's companion, never the guest (Wren checked each sentence, round 6). Red wine is named once, as an ingredient (the Flirt has the family's red). History about 48%. ✓
sources: Studio fact cards `_studio/fact-cards/nellie-bly-amiens.md` (Nellie Bly, *Around the World in Seventy-Two Days*, 1890, chs. I, III, IV, XVIII, primary, University of Pennsylvania transcription) and `_studio/fact-cards/new-york-sour.md` (David Wondrich, *Imbibe!* pdf 96–97; *Oxford Companion* NEW YORK SOUR pdf 1387). Drink: *Oxford Companion* pdf 1049 (the Cock-Tail "at room temperature" until the 1840s); Dave Arnold, *Liquid Intelligence* pp. 51, 104; *Flavor Matrix* GRAPE pdf 140 (consulted, set aside). Runner-up checked on the page: Auguste Levasseur, *Lafayette in America in 1824 and 1825* (1829). Trapier: David Ogg, *South Carolina Historical Magazine* 59:2 (1958). Room notes: `work/lover-hero/`.
names_note: **Out of Your Way**, the room's pick (all three, round 6): they'd go out of their way for anyone they love, and her own record counts "179-1/2 miles out of my way". Under it sits the fear of being in the way. Tomás conceded his *Out of the Way* (a different idiom: a remote place). Also considered: *Raised to You*, *All the Way*, *Both Hands*. *Travel-Stained* stays in the reading only, because on a label the guest would be calling themselves untidy.
open_items: **The plan's lead was overturned in round 1.** Wren ruled that Tudor fails this person: nobody waits for him, the free ice reads as "make them need you", and the brave act is a captain's. The plan backup Trapier was also out (thin on limbs 1–3, a place set and waiting is the Geisha's ground, the julep is the Romantic's). Hester found Bly on the web in round 2. The plan row now notes it.

**The drink is warm, not hot, and has no ice at any point.** It's 20.9% ABV, 4.23 g sugar/100 ml and 0.289% acid, freeform (Arnold has no style for an unchilled drink). The acid is double the stirred band, all of it from the wine, and that edge is owned in Checks. The strength is at fortified-wine level on purpose. The wine is our choice (a young red Bordeaux); the page names no wine and only says "wine and biscuit". It's never the Vernes' claret.

**The drink swapped three times** (rounds 3–5: a cold New York Sour with a red wine float, against this warm toast). Each case is in the room record. The float's history is carded (`new-york-sour.md`) if Robin prefers it.
**The biscuit stays on the page:** beside the glass it would bring gluten, egg and dairy into a veto-free pour.

**Kept out:** the race as the gesture (*Nothing to It*'s and the Explorer family's ground), her rival and her later life, any motive for Verne's rule, "start this minute" (*Off Duty*), any exact date, Bly's Pennsylvania birthplace and rye (a region and era, not her county, and *Brought Home*'s "two places" shape), the 1833 *Transatlantic Sketches* (the Geisha's), and "invented by" for the New York Sour.
**Shape:** Martini · rye · stemmed red wine glass, a triple in no pour or plan. The Lover family now has three Martinis and two Old-Fashioneds.
